shortDescription: Manage C(schematics_workspaces) for Schematics Service API.

options.name: agent_id
options.description: agent id which is binded to with the workspace.

options.name: applied_shareddata_ids
options.description: List of applied shared dataset ID.

options.name: catalog_ref
options.description: Information about the software template that you chose from the IBM Cloud catalog. This information is returned for IBM Cloud catalog offerings only.

options.name: dependencies
options.description: Workspace dependencies.

options.name: description
options.description: The description of the workspace.

options.name: destroy_resources
options.description:
If set to C(true), refreshI(token header configuration is required to delete all the Terraform resources, and the Schematics workspace.
If set to C(false), you can remove only the workspace.
Your Terraform resources are still available and must be managed with the resource dashboard or CLI.

options.name: location
options.description:
The location where you want to create your Schematics workspace and run the Schematics jobs.
The location that you enter must match the API endpoint that you use.
For example, if you use the Frankfurt API endpoint, you must specify C(eu-de) as your location.
If you use an API endpoint for a geography and you do not specify a location, Schematics determines the location based on availability.

options.name: name
options.description:
The name of your workspace. The name can be up to 128 characters long and can include alphanumeric characters, spaces, dashes, and underscores.
When you create a workspace for your own Terraform template,
consider including the microservice component that you set up with your Terraform template and
the IBM Cloud environment where you want to deploy your resources in your name.

options.name: refresh_token
options.description:
The IAM refresh token for the user or service identity.
The IAM refresh token is required only if you want to destroy the Terraform resources before deleting the Schematics workspace.
If you want to delete the workspace only and keep all your Terraform resources, refresh token is not required.
B(Retrieving refresh token)I( Use C(export IBMCLOUDI(API)KEY=<ibmcloudI(api)key>),
and execute C(curl -X POST "https://iam.cloud.ibm.com/identity/token" -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded"

options.name: resource_group
options.description: The ID of the resource group where you want to provision the workspace.

options.name: shared_data
options.description:
Information about the Target used by the templates originating from the IBM Cloud catalog offerings.
This information is not relevant for workspace created using your own Terraform template.

options.name: state
options.description: Should the resource be present or absent.

options.name: tags
options.description: A list of tags that are associated with the workspace.

options.name: template_data
options.description: Input data for the Template.

options.name: template_ref
options.description: Workspace template ref.

options.name: template_repo
options.description: Input variables for the Template repoository, while creating a workspace.

options.name: template_repo_update_request_template_repo
options.displayName: Template Repo Update Request Template Repo
options.description: Input to update the template repository data.

options.name: type
options.description: List of Workspace type.

options.name: w_id
options.description: The ID of the workspace.  To find the workspace ID, use the C(GET /v1/workspaces) API.

options.name: workspace_status
options.description: WorkspaceStatusRequest -.

options.name: workspace_status_msg

options.name: workspace_status_update_request_workspace_status

options.description: The personal access token to authenticate with your private GitHub or GitLab repository and access your Terraform template.
